Math and AT.question: ৪১) A pump can fill a tank with water in 2 hours. Because of a leak, it took 2(1/3) hours to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water of the tank in:
Math and AT.exp:
Question: A pump can fill a tank with water in 2 hours. Because of a leak, it took (7/3) hours to fill the tank. The leak can drain all the water of the tank in:

Solution:
pump fills 1/2 tank in 1 hour 

because of leak, pump fills 3/7 tank in 1 hour 

leak drains (1/2) - (3/7) = 1/14 tank in 1 hour
leak drains full tank in 14 hours

Math and AT.question: ৪২) The least perfect square, which is divisible by each of 21, 36 and 66 is:
Math and AT.exp:
Question: The least perfect square, which is divisible by each of 21, 36 and 66 is-

Solution:
L.C.M. of 21, 36, 66 = 2772.
Now,
2772 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 × 11

To make it a perfect square, it must be multiplied by 7 × 11.
So, required number = 22 × 32 × 72 × 112 = 213444

Math and AT.question: ৪৩) Three times the first of three consecutive odd integers is 3 more than twice the third. The third integer is:
Math and AT.exp:
প্রশ্ন: Three times the first of three consecutive odd integers is 3 more than twice the third. The third integer is:

সমাধান:
Let the three odd integers be x, x + 2 and x + 4.

Then,
3x = 2(x + 4) + 3      
⇒ 3x = 2x + 8 + 3
∴ x = 11

Third integer = x + 4 = 11 + 4 = 15

Math and AT.question: ৪৪) Find the difference between the simple interest and the compound interest at 5% per annum for 2 years on principal of Tk. 2000.
Math and AT.exp:
Question: Find the difference between the simple interest and the compound interest at 5% per annum for 2 years on a principal of Tk 2000.

Solution:
We know, Simple Interest, I = Pnr
and Compound Principal, C = p(1 + r)n

Simple Interest = 2000 × 2 × (5/100) = 200 Tk

Compound Principal = 2000 × {1 + (5/100)}2
= 3000 × (105/100)2
= (3000 × 105 × 110)/(105× 100)
= 2205

So, Compound interest = 2205 - 2000 = 205 Tk

So, difference = 205 - 200 = 5 Tk

Math and AT.question: ৪৫) A and B started a business in partnership investing Tk. 20,000 and Tk. 15,000 respectively. After six months, C joined them with Tk. 20,000. What will be B's share in total profit of Tk. 25,000 earned at the end of 2 years from the starting of the business?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: A and B started a business in partnership investing Tk. 20,000 and Tk. 15,000 respectively. After six months, C joined them with Tk. 20,000. What will be B's share in total profit of Tk. 25,000 earned at the end of 2 years from the starting of the business?

Solution:
Here,
A : B : C
= (20,000 x 24) : (15,000 x 24) : (20,000 x 18)
= 4 : 3 : 3.
So, B's share = 25000 x 3/10 = 7,500.

Math and AT.question: ৪৮) Waking 3/4 of his normal speed, Rabi is 16 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and office:
Math and AT.exp:
প্রশ্ন:Waking 3/4 of his normal speed, Rabi is 16 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and office:

সমাধান: 
Let,
The usual speed be S.
New speed = S × (3/4)
⇒ The ratio of usual speed to new speed = 4 : 3
∴ The ratio of the usual time to new time = 3 : 4

Let,
His usual time be 3x and the new time is 4x.
Difference in time = 4x - 3x = 16 mins
⇒ x = 16 mins

The usual time taken = 3x
= 3 × 16 = 48 mins
∴ The usual time to reach the office is 48 mins.

Math and AT.question: ৪৯) Find the average of first 97 natural numbers.
Math and AT.exp:
Question: Find the average of first 20 consecutive natural numbers.

Solution:
The average of first n consecutive natural numbers is
=(n + 1)/2

Here,
n=97

So, average = (97+1)/2
= 98/2
= 49

Math and AT.question: ৫০) How many kilogram of sugar costing Tk. 9 per kg must be mixed with 27 kg of sugar costing Tk. 7 per kg so that there may be a gain of 10% by selling the mixture at Tk. 9.24 per kg?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: How many kilogram of sugar costing Tk. 9 per kg must be mixed with 27 kg of sugar costing Tk. 7 per kg so that there may be a gain of 10% by selling the mixture at Tk. 9.24 per kg?

Solution:
Let, the sugar of Tk 9 per kg is = x kg

ATQ,
110% of (7 × 27 + 9 × x) = 9.24(27 + x)
⇒ (11/10) × (189 + 9x) = 249.48 + 9.24x
⇒ 2079 + 99x = 2494.8 + 92.4x
⇒ 6.6x = 415.8
⇒ x = 63

Math and AT.question: ৫১) A person's present age is two-fifth of the age of his mother. After 8 years, he will be one-half of the age of his mother. How old is the mother at present?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: A person's present age is two-fifth of the age of his mother. After 8 years, he will be one-half of the age of his mother what is the present age of the mother?

Solution: 
Let the age of the person’s mother be ‘x’ units.
So, age of the person = (2x/5)
After 8 years, age of the person’s mother = ‘x + 8’ units.
So age of the person after 8 years = (2x/5) + 8 
According to question:
(2x/5) + 8 = (a + 8)/2
=> (2x + 40)/5 = (a + 8)/2
=> 4a + 80 = 5a + 40
 =>5a - 4a = 80 - 40
=> a = 40

So, the present age of his mother is 40 years.

Math and AT.question: ৫২) A person sold a horse at a gain of 15%. Had he bought it for 25% less and sold it for Tk. 600 less, he would have made a profit of 32%. The cost price of the horse was?
Math and AT.exp:
Question:  A person sold a horse at a gain of 15%. Had he bought it for 25% less and sold it for Tk. 600 less, he would have made a profit of 32%. The cost price of the horse was?
Solution:
Let the original cost price = Tk. x

Selling price = x + 15% of x
= 115x/100
= 23x/20

Cost price = x - 25% of x
= x - (25x/100)
= 75x/100
= 3x/4

Selling price = (3x/4) + 32% of (3x/4)
= (3x/4) + (32/100) × (3x/4)
= 99x/100

ATQ,
(23x/20) - (99x/100) = 600
⇒ (115x - 99x)/100 = 600
⇒ 16x = 600 × 100
⇒ x = (600 × 100)/16
∴ x = 3750

Math and AT.question: ৫৩) If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days while 26 men and 48 boys can do the same in 2 days, the time taken by 15 men and 20 boys in doing the same type of work will be-
Math and AT.exp:
Let 1 man's 1 day's work = x
and 1 boy's 1 day's work = y.
Then,
6x + 8y = 1/10 and
26 x + 48y = 1/2
Solving these two questions, we get,
x = 1/100 and
y = 1/200
(15 men + 20 boys)'s 1 day's work = (15/100 + 20/200)
= 1/4

1/4 portion of work is done in 1 day
Full work is done in 4 days

∴ 15 men and 20 boys can do the work in 4 days.

Math and AT.question: ৫৪) The average temperature for Wednesday, Thursday and Friday was 40ᵒC. The average for Thursday, Friday and Saturday was 41ᵒC. If temperature on Saturday was 42ᵒC, what was the temperature on Wednesday?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: The average temperature for Wednesday, Thursday and Friday was 40°C. The average for Thursday, Friday and Saturday was 41°C. If temperature on Saturday was 42°C, what was the temperature on Wednesday?

Solution:
Here,
Total temperature for Wednesday, Thursday and Friday = 3 × 40° = 120°C
Total temperature for Thursday, Friday and Saturday = 3 × 41° = 123°C

Now,
(Thursday + Friday + Saturday) - (Wednesday + Thursday + Friday) = 123° - 120°
⇒ Saturday - Wednesday = 3°
∴ Wednesday = 42° - 3° = 39°C

Math and AT.question: ৫৫) A dishonest shopkeeper sells his grocery using weights 10% less than true weights and makes a profit of 30%. Find his total gain percentage.
Math and AT.exp:
Let
the weight of the grocery bag be 1000 gm.
Now, the shopkeeper sells his grocery using weights 10% less than true weights.
Hence, actual weight of bag = 90% of 1000 gm = 900 gm
If each gram = Tk.1, C.P. of each bag containing 900 gm = Tk. 900
The shopkeeper sells with a gain of 30% on true C.P.

Calculate the S.P.
Selling price = 100 + gain% × C.P.
Therefore,
Selling price = (130/100) × Tk. 1000
= Tk. 1300
Gain = S.P. - C.P. = 1300 - 900 = Tk. 400
Gain% = (400/900) × 100
= 44.44%

Math and AT.question: ৫৬) A tank is filled by three pipes with uniform flow. The first two pipes operating simultaneously fill the tank in the same time during which the tank is filled by the third pipe alone. The second pipe fills the tank 5 hours faster than the first pipe and 4 hours slower than the third pipe. The time required by the first pipe is?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: A tank is filled by three pipes with uniform flow. The first two pipes operating simultaneously fill the tank in the same time during which the tank is filled by the third pipe alone. The second pipe fills the tank 5 hours faster than the first pipe and 4 hours slower than the third pipe. The time required by the first pipe is-

Solution:
Suppose, first pipe alone takes x hours to fill the tank .
Then, second and third pipes will take (x - 5) and (x - 9) hours respectively to fill the tank.

ATQ,
1/x + 1/(x - 5) = 1/(x - 9)
⇒ (x - 5 + x)/x(x - 5) = 1/(x - 9)
⇒ (2x - 5)(x - 9) = x(x - 5)
⇒ x2 - 18x + 45 = 0
⇒ x2 - 15x - 3x + 45 = 0
⇒ x(x - 15) - 3(x - 15) = 0
⇒ (x - 15)(x - 3) = 0
∴ x = 15 [neglecting x = 3]

Math and AT.question: ৫৭) How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in a day?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: How many times the hands of a clock coincide in a day?

Solution:
The hands of a clock coincide only once between 11 O'clock and 1 O'clock,
So in every 12 hours, the hands of a clock will coincide for 11 times.

∴ In a day or 24 hours, the hands of a clock will coincide for 22 (11 + 11) times.

Math and AT.question: ৫৯) If A and B together can complete a work in 18 days, A and C together in 12 days, and B and C together in 9 days, then B alone can do the work in?
Math and AT.exp:
A and B together can complete a work in 18 days
A and B together can complete 1/18 part of a work in 1 days

A and C together can complete a work in 12 days
A and C together can complete 1/12 part of a work in 1 days

B and C together can complete a work in 9 days
B and C together can complete 1/9 part of a work in 1 days

A, B and C together can complete (1/9 + 1/12 + 1/18)/2 part or 1/8 part of a work in 1 days

1 day's work of B = 1/8 - 1/12 = 1/24
B alone can do the work in 24 days

Math and AT.question: ৬০) In triangle PQR length of the side QR is less than twice the length of the side PQ by 2 cm. Length of the side PR exceeds the length of the side PQ by 10 cm. The perimeter is 40 cm. What is the length of the smallest side of the triangle PQR?
Math and AT.exp:
In △PQR,
QR + 2 = 2PQ
QR = 2PQ - 2 ..........(1)
PR = PQ + 10 ......... (2)
Perimeter = 40 m
Or, PQ + QR + RP = 40
Putting the value of PQ and QR from equation (1) and (2),
PQ + 2PQ - 2 + PQ + 10 = 40
Or, 4PQ = 32
Or, PQ = 8 cm ,which is the smallest side of the triangle.

Math and AT.question: ৬১) A train passes a station platform in 36 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 20 seconds. If the speed of the train is 54 km/hr, what is the length of the platform?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: A train passes a station platform in 36 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 20 seconds. If the speed of the train is 54 km/hr, what is the length of the platform?

Solution:
Speed = (54 × 1000)/3600 
= 15 m/sec

Length of the train = (15 × 20) m = 300 m
Let
the length of the platform be x meters.

Then,
(x + 300)/36 = 15
⇒ x + 300 = 540
∴ x = 240 meters

Math and AT.question: ৬২) The length of a rectangle is halved, while its breadth is tripled. What is the percentage change in area?
Math and AT.exp:
Let original length = 10
original breadth = 10
Then, original area = 10 × 10 = 100
Length is halved
⇒ New length = 10/2
= 5
breadth is tripled.
⇒ New breadth = 10 × 3
= 30
New area = 5 × 30
= 150
Increase in area
= new area - original area
= 150 - 100
= 50
Percentage increase in area
= {(increase in area/original area) × 100}%
= {(50/100) × 100}%
= 50%.

Math and AT.question: ৬৩) The greatest number of four digits which is divisible by 15, 25, 40 and 75 is:
Math and AT.exp:
Greatest number of four digits = 9999
LCM of 15, 25, 40 and 75 = 600
9999/600 = 16,
remainder = 399
Hence, greatest number of four digits which is divisible by 15, 25, 40 and 75
= 9999 - 399
= 9600

Math and AT.question: ৬৪) A man can row three-quarters of a kilometre against the stream in 11.25 minutes and down the stream in 7.5 minutes. The speed (in km/hr) of the man in still water is:
Math and AT.exp:
Question: A man can row three-quarters of a kilometre against the stream in 11.25 minutes and down the stream in 7.5 minutes. The speed (in km/hr) of the man in still water is:

Solution:
Three - quarters of a kilometer = (3 × 1000)/4 meters = 750 meters

11.25 minutes = 11.25 × 60 = 675 sec
7.5 minutes = 7.5 × 60 = 450sec

Rate upstream = 750/ 675 m/sec
= 10/9 m/sec

Rate downstream =750/450 m/sec
 = 5/3 m/sec


∴Rate in still water = (1/2){(10/9) + (5/3)} m/sec
= (1/2){(10 + 15)/9}
= (1/2)(25/9)
= 25/18
= (25/18)(18/5) km/hr.
= 5 km/hr

Math and AT.question: ৬৫) Tickets numbered 1 to 20 are mixed up and then a ticket is drawn at random. What is the probability that the ticket drawn has a number which is a multiple of 3 or 5?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: Tickets numbered 1 to 20 are mixed up and then a ticket is drawn at random. What is the probability that the ticket drawn has a number which is a multiple of 3 or 5?

Solution:
Total number of tickets = 20

The numbers which are multiple of 3 or 5 are {3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20}
∴ Total expected events = 9

∴ The probability = 9/20

Math and AT.question: ৬৬)  In a class of 65 students and 4 teachers, each student got sweets that are 20% of the total number of students and each teacher got sweets that are 40% of the total number of students. How many sweets are there?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: In a class of 65 students and 4 teachers, each student got sweets that are 20% of the total number of students and each teacher got sweets that are 40% of the total number of students. How many sweets are there?

Solution:
There are 65 students and 4 teachers
Each student got sweets that are 20% of the total number of students.
So each student got sweets = 65 × 20%
= 13 sweets.

∴ Total sweets for students is = 65 × 13 = 845

Each teacher got sweets that are 40% of the total number of students.
So each teacher got sweets = 65 × 40% = 26 sweets.

There are 4 teachers, so total sweets for teachers = 4 × 26 = 104

∴ Total sweets = sweets for students + sweets for teachers
= 845 + 104
= 949

Therefore, the total number of sweets is 949.

Math and AT.question: ৬৭) A runs twice as fast as B and B runs thrice as fast as C. The distance covered by C in 72 minutes, will be covered by A in :
Math and AT.exp:
Question: A runs twice as fast as B and B runs thrice as fast as C. The distance covered by C in 72 minutes, will be covered by A in :

Solution:
Let C's speed = x km/hr
Then, B's speed = 3x km/hr
And A's speed = 6x km/hr
∴ Ratio of speeds of A, B, C
= 6x : 3x : x
= 6 : 3 : 1
Ratio of times taken
= 1/6 : 1/3 : 1
= 1 : 2 : 6

If C takes 6 minutes, then A takes 1 minute
If C takes 72 minutes, then A takes (1/6) × 72 min = 12 min

Math and AT.question: ৬৮) Vendor sells apples at a certain price in order to make a profit of 30%. If he charges Tk. 1.5 higher per apple he would get a profit of 60%. Find the original price at which he sold an apple?
Math and AT.exp:
Question: Vendor sells apples at a certain price in order to make a profit of 30%. If he charges Tk. 1.5 higher per apple he would get a profit of 60%. Find the original price at which he sold an apple? 

Solution: 
Cost price of an apple = Tk. x 
and original selling price = selling price at 30% profit = 130% of x = Tk. 1.3x
Again at 60% profit selling price = 160% of x = Tk. 1.6x

ATQ,
1.6x = x + 1.5
⇒ 1.6x - x = 1.5
⇒ .6x = 1.5
⇒ x = 1.5/.6
∴ x = 2.5

Hence, original selling price = 1.3x = Tk. (1.5 × 2.5) = Tk. 3.25

Math and AT.question: ৭০) A is twice good a workman as B and therefore is able to finish a job in 30 days less than B. Working together they can do it in -
Math and AT.exp:
Question: A is twice good a workman as B and therefore is able to finish a job in 30 days less than B. Working together they can do it in -

Solution:
Let B can do the work in x days.
A can do the work in (x - 30) days.
A is twice efficient as compared to B.
(x - 30) = x/2
x = 60 days

B can do the work in 60 days while A can do the work in 30 days.

Total time taken by A and B together to complete the work = 1/(1/60 + 1/30)
= 20 days
